messages:
maria: Quick sync 1: need a compact probe policy for intake when bench budget is constrained. Goal: a minimal set that reliably flags the most common runtime regressions (latency, tokenization, kv warming).

sam: Sounds good. My instinct is a FAST smoke that runs everywhere: p95 latency, kv-cache hit sanity, tokenizer diff check. Keep it deterministic and quick. :thumbsup:

jon: Add a tiny correctness smoke too  maybe 20 fixed prompts against golden outputs to capture decode/serialization hiccups. Very low cost but high signal.

maria: Proposal: categorize probes as FAST (<=45s), MID (5-12m), DEEP (>30m). FAST runs on every submit; MID on config/tokenizer/model-arch changes or sampled; DEEP offline nightly or for major releases. Agree?

eva: +1 to tiers. FAST should include a cold-start trace (first N tokens p50/p95) since cold-start regressions sneak through often.

sam: FAST invariants: deterministic (no sampling), fixed seed, short seqlen (<=64), single-thread runner to avoid noisy variance.

jon: For MID, suggest ~200 stratified golden inputs split across seqlen bins and content types (code, dialogue, prose). Good balance of quality signal vs cost.

maria: Draft intake selection rules: 
```
if changes.tokenizer or model.arch_change:
  run MID
elif changes.quantization or compile_flag:
  run FAST + 10% sampled MID
else:
  run FAST
```
If FAST fails -> auto-promote to MID and block until triage. Thoughts?

sam: That escalation sounds right. Make promotion explicit and surface artifacts. Don't silently mark as OK.

jon: Also need fallback for infra-limited MID runs: if MID OOMs on target pool, automatically rerun MID on smaller-batch/quantized variant and flag onboarding as "needs-review".

maria: Observability: standardize metric names so Console can compare across models: latency_p95_ms, coldstart_p95_ms, kv_miss_rate, tokenizer_diff_count, golden_mismatch_count.

eva: Include provenance: probe_version, code_sha, runner_image, hardware_profile, golden_set_id. That's key for debugging flakiness.

sam: Implementation sketch for FAST runner: 
```
run_probe --kind fast --seq-len 32 --seed 42 --prompts fast_prompts.json --out metrics.json
```
Expect exit 0 and metrics.json with fields: latency_p95_ms, kv_miss_rate, tokenizer_diff_count. Non-zero -> upload logs/artifacts.

maria: We need a quick fast_prompts.json that hits short convo, code snippet, whitespace edgecases, unicode symbols, and tokenization boundaries. Who can author ~40 prompts?

jon: I can assemble 40 prompts and push to ml-goldsets/fast_smoke/ tomorrow. Will include explicit expected outputs for the golden-check.

probe-bot: probe-bot: latest FAST run: latency_p95_ms=38, coldstart_p95_ms=72, kv_miss_rate=0.015, tokenizer_diff_count=0, golden_mismatch_count=0. :white_check_mark:

maria: Great. Next steps: I'll open a short RFC to formalize tiers, intake rules, metric schema, artifact locations, and the FAST failure runbook (promote->block->triage). Aiming to circulate by EOD.

sam: Please include SLO thresholds so alerts can be colored in Console. Suggested FAST SLOs: latency_p95_ms < 100, coldstart_p95_ms < 200, kv_miss_rate < 0.05, tokenizer_diff_count == 0.

jon: MID thresholds will be looser for quality but we should define variability windows and regression detection logic.

maria: Thanks all  tagging @sam @jon @eva for review once RFC lands. :eyes:

probe-bot: probe-bot: artifact stored at s3://redwood-probes/1768612345/fast/metrics.json

maria: perfect, that'll be referenced in the RFC.
